meta.title: Outlander
sources: Ronald D. Moore adapting Diana Gabaldon (2014–)

worlds.label: Claire/Jamie continuum via standing stones
worlds.description: Soft Novikov: big history resists; personal lives contingent

events.label: Claire and Frank honeymoon in Highlands
events.description: In 1945, former combat nurse Claire Randall honeymoon in the Scottish Highlands with the husband she was separated from by the war.

events.label: Craigh na Dun stones displace Claire to 1743
events.description: At the stone circle of Craigh na Dun, Claire touches the standing stones - and is thrown through two hundred years into the Scotland of 1743.

events.label: Arrives 1743 Scotland
events.description: Claire wakes in the middle of the eighteenth century, a woman out of time in a country at war with itself.

events.label: Meets Jamie Fraser
events.description: She meets Jamie Fraser, a young Highlander who shelters her from the hands of a brutal English officer - the beginning of the bond the whole story turns on.

events.label: Marries Jamie for protection
events.description: To keep her from that officer's clutches, Claire marries Jamie - a marriage of convenience that stops being convenient as real love takes root.

events.label: Frank searches in 1940s
events.description: In 1945 and after, Frank searches for his vanished wife through years that never explain her.

events.label: Claire's history knowledge of Culloden
events.description: Claire carries the future in her head: she knows the Jacobite cause dies at Culloden in 1746, and knows the history books' verdict in advance.

events.label: Attempts to alter Jacobite outcomes
events.description: She tries to use that knowledge - to warn, to change, to save - and finds two centuries of recorded history a heavy thing to push against.

events.label: Separations / return stones temptation
events.description: Across the story, the pull of the stones never stops: Claire is repeatedly torn between two centuries and the two lives she has in them.

events.label: Claire returns to 20th century pregnant
events.description: Pregnant and despairing, Claire returns through the stones to the twentieth century - to Frank, and to a life spent half elsewhere.

events.label: Brianna born; raised with Frank
events.description: She gives birth to Jamie's daughter, Brianna, and raises her with Frank in the centuries between.

events.label: Years later research Jamie survival
events.description: Twenty years on, Claire - now a doctor - finds historical proof that Jamie survived Culloden.

events.label: Claire returns to 18th c. to Jamie
events.description: With Brianna grown, Claire goes back through the stones again - to 1766 and the man she left.

events.label: Reunion with Jamie
events.description: The reunion: Jamie the printer, alive, grey-streaked - and the two of them picking up a marriage two hundred interrupted years old.

events.label: Brianna and Roger also travel via stones
events.description: Brianna and Roger follow her parents into the past through the same stones, adding their own thread to the family's time-crossed story.

events.label: Multi-generational Fraser timeline entanglement
events.description: The saga's spine: one family, scattered across three centuries, holding together by letters, names and stones.

events.label: History resists large changes; personal mutable
events.description: The rule as the story learns it: great history holds its shape - battles happen, plagues come - but private lives have room to bend.

events.label: Other travelers (Geillis) confirm mechanism
events.description: Another traveller, Geillis Duncan, proves to Claire she is not alone - and that the stones have been moving people for centuries.

events.label: New World arcs continue displacement theme
events.description: The story crosses to the New World, where the Fraser family's American chapters begin - displacement by ocean now, not just by stone.

events.label: Cross-time letters / evidence bridges eras
events.description: Letters and records across the centuries become the family's bridge - evidence posted between eras by people who know where the post-boxes really are.

events.label: Love as reason to stay despite paradox risk
events.description: The choice the story keeps making concrete: Claire chooses the past, and Jamie, over the safety of her own century - love as the reason to stay.

events.label: Ongoing stone-travel family saga
events.description: The saga continues as it always has: a family living out of order, bound by stones, love and two hundred years of proof.

ruleEffects.effect: Personal fates feel drawn despite attempts to warn

outcome.summary: Standing stones displace Claire between 1940s and 1740s; family later multi-travels; history resists macro change.
